### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via enforceProjectMembership (symbol, a method of class HttpDispatcher))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **155** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5b3a41f29167da67e9c28ec3fb623d3282fde317` — the merge of head `05c1551ce7b76609b6b9923c5a890a9aa2858afa` into base `6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5b3a41f29167da67e9c28ec3fb623d3282fde317 && git checkout 5b3a41f29167da67e9c28ec3fb623d3282fde317
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228 05c1551ce7b76609b6b9923c5a890a9aa2858afa && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228 && git merge --no-ff 05c1551ce7b76609b6b9923c5a890a9aa2858afa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e43b7bc3f8cec05e65e200f28c9e6074c585228` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `05c1551ce7b76609b6b9923c5a890a9aa2858afa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-admin-gate.undefined-direction.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-session-principal.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-no-active-organization.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-outbox-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-organization-stamping.test.ts, .changeset/24222-get-session-readers-declared.md, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/actor-user.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts

PR #24232 for card #24222, isolated at-tier review, read-only. The head is a merge of `origin/main` `9040945d` into the dev branch (two non-merge commits, `3f0e6ed29` and `6f351e9bf`); the net diff against that merge base is 15 files, +231/-44, and matches GitHub's PR diff hunk for hunk. The head had not moved when read; `origin/main` has since advanced one commit (`7715d049e`, PR #24234, `packages/cli` only, no overlap). Inputs: the card body and its three comments (triage `6241789224`, claim `6242034533`, dev report `6243590371`), the PR body, file list and diff, the head's 41 check-runs, and the cited code read at the head. The scope above is the contract file (the one `reviewFace` hit) plus every file its hunks make a claim about: the new docblock paragraph claims every other in-process reader, so the whole diff is in scope, and the last seven paths are read-only producers and readers consulted to judge that claim (the `customSession` producer, the `name` reader's consumer, and the five `getSession` call sites the card never named). No remainder is left to a lane ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface, one change: `AuthSessionApi.getSession`'s result gains three optional `user` members. Each one judged against the reader named on it, read at the head:

- `user.isPlatformAdmin: boolean` (optional) — right. The producer is plugin-auth's `customSession` (`auth-manager.ts`): `let platformAdmin = false`, then `platformAdmin = grants.posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` inside a `try` whose `catch` leaves it `false`, returned as `user: { ...user, positions, isPlatformAdmin: platformAdmin, ... }`. A boolean, `false` when not held, as the docblock says. The reader is `judgePlatformAdmin` through `isPlatformAdminUser` (`u.isPlatformAdmin === true`), which admits on `true` alone.
- `user.role: string | null` (optional) — right. better-auth 1.7.3 (the version plugin-auth pins) declares the admin plugin's column `role: { type: 'string', required: false, input: false }` and types it `role?: string | undefined` on `UserWithRole`; `sys_user` is `managedBy: 'better-auth'` and declares no `role` field of its own, so the vendor schema is the authority on the column and `required: false` is what makes the `null` arm real. The contract's `string | null` is wider than the implementer's own type, the sound direction for an implementer, and the same call the #24196 review (`6240835611`) made for `impersonatedBy`. The reader narrows with `u.role === 'admin'`, so `null` and `undefined` both refuse.
- `user.name: string` (optional) — right. Read at `dispatcher-plugin.ts:2322`, `displayName: sessionData?.user?.name`, into `buildActorUser` (`actor-user.ts:188`, `displayName?: string`), with `sessionData` from `resolveSessionData`, which this PR types. The read existed on `main` under `any`; removing the `any` made it TS2339, which is how it surfaced. The card did not name it, but the dispatch's file surface names `dispatcher-plugin.ts` as a reader, and the hold-off is "any field no reader reads", which this is not. better-auth's core `User.name` is a required `string`, so the optional declaration is wider than the implementer. Decided as item 1 of ③.

Nothing undeclared is read by any typed reader. Every read at the head, per site: plugin-auth's four mounts read `user.id`, `user.email`, `user.authGate` (through `judgeHeldSession` to `evaluateAuthGate`), `user.isPlatformAdmin` and `user.role`; `has-permission` reads `user.id` and `isPlatformAdminUser(user)`, its former `{ user?: { id?: unknown } }` cast gone. REST reads `gatedSession?.user` into `normalizeAuthGate`, and its closure feeds `resolveAuthzContext` (declared reads, #24196). Runtime: `readGatedSessionUser` returns `session?.user` as `unknown`; `resolveSessionPrincipalId` reads `user.id` and `session.userId`; the AI-route resolver reads `user.id`, `session.userId`, `user.name`, `user.email`, `session.activeOrganizationId`; `enforceAuthGate` reads `session?.user` into `evaluateAuthGate`; `enforceProjectMembership` reads `user.id`, `session.userId`, `session.activeOrganizationId`. Cloud-connection reads `user.id` and `user` (posture), and hands `readFrom.sessionData` back as a `getSession` thunk to `resolveAuthzContext` (`:435`); install-local's `resolveActiveOrgId` reads `session.activeOrganizationId` and its bridge closure feeds `resolveAuthzContext`. Webhooks reads `user`, `user.id`, `session.activeOrganizationId` (`:547`, `:551`, `:580`). Storage reads `user.id` and `session.activeOrganizationId` (upload stamp), `session?.user` (gate reader), and its closure feeds `resolveAuthzContext` (file-read authorizer). All declared.

The docblock's new sentence is universal ("the other in-process readers read the result as declared here too; none reads a top-level `activeOrganizationId`"), so it was judged against the full census of `inProcessSessionReadInput` call sites at the head (20 non-test sites), not the card's list. Five sites the card never named: `plugin-hono-server/current-user-endpoints.ts:477`, `plugin-sharing/sharing-plugin.ts:948` and `service-datasource/admin-routes.ts:223` bind `api` through `IAuthService` or `AuthSessionApi`, so their result is already the declared type (hono reads `user.id` and hands the session to `resolveAuthzContext`; the other two read no field). `service-settings/settings-service-plugin.ts:308` and `runtime/security/resolve-execution-context.ts:183` still build `api` as `any`, but each is a pass-through closure that reads no field and hands the result to `resolveAuthzContext`, whose reads are declared. The sentence therefore holds for what it claims, field reads; the two `any` handles are a handle-typing matter held out by the dispatch's hold-offs, not a reader outside the contract. The three other spreads of the helper (`createOAuthClient`, `addMember`, `setPassword`) are not session reads. After the two removals, every remaining `session?.activeOrganizationId` read in the tree is off better-auth's session ROW inside plugin-auth's own hooks and audit (`auth-manager.ts:1387`, `:7971`, `auth-session-audit.ts:141`, `:165`), never off a `getSession` result. True as written.

The vendor binding at the four plugin-auth mounts: `AuthManager.getApi()` answers a `Promise` of better-auth's own `Auth['api']` (options generic `any`), and each mount now assigns that read to `SessionRead | null` with no cast. CI's `Type Check · workspace` leg (success) proves the assignment holds; the dev's probe (assigning the read to `number` fails naming the vendor's concrete `{ session, user } | null` type) is what shows the binding is not `any`, reported and consistent with the green legs, not reproduced here. What the type check cannot do, by the card's own design (every member optional, so an absent property is assignable): catch a vendor or `customSession` rename of `isPlatformAdmin` or `role` at compile time. The compensating control triage asked for is present: `platform-admin-gate.undefined-direction.test.ts` pins six refusing signals (both absent, both explicitly `undefined`, `role: null`, `isPlatformAdmin: false`, the string `'true'`, `'Admin'`) through `isPlatformAdminUser` (false) and `judgePlatformAdmin` (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, every user carrying an `id` so the 401 cannot mask the 403), plus two admitting controls. Right.

`judgePlatformAdmin(session: unknown)` keeps its `unknown` parameter and reads `(session as SessionRead | null)?.user` — right: the function is a published `@objectstack/plugin-auth` export, narrowing it would be an input narrowing inside a widening card, the same call the #24196 review made for `ResolveAuthzInput.getSession`. The cast is to the contract type, so what the judge reads is checked against the declaration, while the mounts bind the vendor type to it uncast. `isPlatformAdminUser(sessionUser: unknown)` stays for raw user rows (`admin-impersonate-endpoint.ts`) — right.

Accept sets: one runtime behaviour change, the removal of the top-level `activeOrganizationId` operand at `storage-service-plugin.ts:1191` and `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3370`. Producers: the only in-tree `auth` service is `AuthManager`; its read is better-auth's `getSession` under `customSession`, answering `{ user, session }`; `AuthSessionApi` on `main` already declared no top-level member; the only in-tree claims for the flattened shape were a storage code comment and a test fixture naming no producer. Prime Directive #12 wants a bare fallback for an off-contract shape removed or declared as a conversion; the card's Done-when and triage both sanctioned removal. Pins: the storage fixture is flipped to `{ context: { isSystem: true } }`, byte-identical to the declared no-active-organization case at `:393` (ADR-0123 D1), so a flattened payload now lands exactly as "no active organization"; install-local gains the `topLevelOrg` case, 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` naming the missing active organization with `loadCalls` empty. The dev's ablation (operand restored, both pins red) is reported, not reproduced. Right.

Every other hunk is type-only, checked branch by branch: `resolveSessionData` keeps the same `api` then `getApi()` sequence, now through `IAuthService`'s declared members; `has-permission` keeps `user?.id && isPlatformAdminUser(user)`; REST, both `HttpDispatcher` reads, webhooks and storage keep their `try`/`catch` shapes and the `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` relays unchanged.

Published surfaces of the six consumer packages: unchanged. `SessionRead` is module-local in all nine new copies (none exported); `resolveSessionData`'s return type moves from a `Promise` of `any` to `SessionRead | null`, and it is module-internal (`runtime/src/index.ts` does not export it, the package exports only `.`, and its one caller is `dispatcher-plugin.ts`); `resolveSession` (webhooks) is private, `buildGetSession` (storage) and `ResolvedSession` (cloud-connection) are unexported; `judgePlatformAdmin`'s signature is unchanged.

Generated artifacts: no Zod schema, no `.describe()`, no export added or removed, so no api-surface, json-schema, docs or authorable-surface artifact moves (the api-surface snapshot records that an export exists, not an interface's optional members); the dev reports `check:generated` exit 0 before and after the merge, and the `Type Check · source gates` leg that carries its reconcile is success. Docs: the drift check names `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx` through `enforceProjectMembership`, whose only change is the typed binding, and `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx` names `AuthSessionApi` on its `api?` and `getApi?` lines without restating the result shape. Nothing owed.

One cosmetic note for the lane, not a contract matter: in `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts` the alias sits between two `import` statements (`:20`, ahead of `import { SysWebhook }`); `Lint · ESLint` is success.

Gate verdicts on the head, read off the check-runs (theirs, not this record's): all 41 completed. The required five are success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (all four legs success), `Test Core` (aggregate and all six shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (no governed path in the file list). Also success: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, the card-claim, single-writer and part-of checks, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregate). The full-battery jobs (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, the dogfood shards, `Build Docs`) are `skipped` on a PR run by design.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24222-get-session-readers-declared.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`; `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `rest`, `runtime`, `cloud-connection`, `plugin-webhooks`, `service-storage`: `patch`. Right. Spec widens a published contract's result type, which is `minor`, the floor a `Clause-②: yes` line demands. plugin-auth, rest, runtime and webhooks change no exported surface and no runtime behaviour, type-only reader edits in released packages, so `patch`, never `skip-changeset`. service-storage and cloud-connection carry the one behaviour change, and it is not a `(narrowing)` arm: the set that moved was never published. `AuthSessionApi` on `main` already declared no top-level member, `IAuthService` is the only declared producer handle, and the tolerance lived in a consumer `??` and a fixture naming no producer. Removing a bare fallback for an off-contract shape is Prime Directive #12's prescribed direction and the card's Done-when, so it is a fix in a released package, `patch`, and the changeset body carries the consumer-facing sentence (what an auth service that answered only the flattened shape now gets, and the one-line remedy: answer it on `session.activeOrganizationId`). Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed; `check:adr-0087-registration` rides `Lint & Repo Gates`, success. The `Clause-②` line reads `yes (widening)` on the changeset and `yes` on the PR body, the same declaration said two ways (`clause2-line.mjs`), both truthful: a declaration widening, no narrowing anywhere in the diff. `Check Changeset` is success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry from report `6243590371`:

1. open_question — keep `user.name` in this PR (A) or split it off and leave the reader on a cast (B)? Answered: A, as shipped. The card's Done-when is "it reads through the declared result, with each field it reads declared for it", and `dispatcher-plugin.ts` is on the dispatch's file surface; B would leave exactly the cast the card exists to remove. One optional member whose reader is measured (`:2322`) and whose producer is better-auth's core `User.name`, the least rename-prone field on the result. The recommendation stands.
2. open_question — export one `SessionRead` alias from `@objectstack/spec/contracts` (B) or keep the module-local copies (A)? Answered: A. No external reader pulls for it, an export is an api-surface entry and a commitment to one public spelling, and every copy is derived from the contract, so none can drift from it. A correction for the record: the head carries eleven copies, not nine — two from #24196 (`core/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `service-print/print-routes.ts`) and nine from this diff (`platform-admin-gate.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `http-dispatcher.ts`, `resolve-session-principal.ts`, `cloud-connection-plugin.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts`, `storage-service-plugin.ts`). An exported alias becomes its own card on a named external reader; not this one.
3. deviation — the harness attribution reminder versus the model-free trailer pair: both non-merge commits (`3f0e6ed29`, `6f351e9bf`) carry the model-free `Claude-Session:` and `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair the rule requires. Resolved.
4. deviation — the PR was not subscribed to CI (os-dev contract): no review consequence; the gate verdicts are read off the head above.
5. deviation — `test:repo` run for spec, rest and runtime beyond os-dev's default: no rule broken, no consequence.
6. deviation — the first build's TS2339 on `user.name`: the organic red that produced the `name` declaration; it is in the diff and is item 1. Closed.
7. `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, shallow clone): `Lint & Repo Gates` carries it and is success on the head. Closed.
8. out_of_scope_finding, "carrier: none, not filed" — `cloud-connection-plugin.ts:316` resolves the handle as `getApi()`, then `authSvc.api`, then `authSvc` itself. Confirmed at the head, and the only operand of that shape in the tree. It is a bare fallback treating the auth service as its own session handle, a shape `IAuthService` does not declare: the same Prime Directive #12 class as the operand this card removed, one level up (the handle rather than the result). Reach: inert against any `IAuthService`-conformant service (`getApi` or `api` resolves first), and against a bare service with no `getSession` it answers `null`, no session, so it admits nothing it should not; it only matters for a host registering a bare session api as `auth`, which no in-tree producer does. Held out of this card by the dispatch's hold-off ("any runtime behaviour change at a reader beyond the two top-level operands"), so correctly left. Escalated, not blocking: the seat files one follow-up card to remove the operand or name its producer, with a pin beside it. This reviewer's one write channel is this comment.

The card's other route ("typed by better-auth's own handle on purpose, and says so") was taken nowhere; every named reader took the declared result. No governed path in the file list; the PR is a draft with auto-merge unarmed; the head repository is the base repository, so this is a delivery, not a fork proposal. The dev is a cloud session (`session_018fKVdiy1mpvMbYt2ryCsLz`) distinct from the reviewing session below, so the independence pair holds.
